title: Classroom Practice — Reading: Math in the Garden
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: Read about Jayda as she uses math to plan a garden in her grandma's backyard. Read each part, then choose the best answer.

sections.title: Math in the Garden
sections.directions: You will take a reading test in English. First, read each part of the story. Then answer the question by choosing the best answer. Read carefully — you can read each part more than once.

items.title: A garden in the backyard
passage: This is Jayda. She is going to make a garden in her grandma's backyard.

options.text: rows of plants someone is watering

items.correct: Correct — a garden has plants growing in the ground.
items.hint: Where do fruits and vegetables grow?

items.title: The shape of the garden
passage: Jayda is going to plant flowers, fruits, and vegetables. First she must decide how big to make her garden. She uses string to plan how long and wide it will be. She decides to make it in the shape of a rectangle so she can plant the most flowers, fruits, and vegetables.
items.prompt: Which picture shows the shape that Jayda plans to make the garden?
items.hint: Reread the last sentence of the part above.

items.title: Inside the shape
passage: Next, Jayda needs to figure out how big the inside of the garden will be.
items.prompt: If she is trying to figure out how big the inside of the shape is, what is this called?
items.correct: Correct — the space inside a shape is the area.
items.hint: Which word means the space inside a flat shape?

items.title: Size of the garden
passage: Jayda has picked the shape for her garden and now she is figuring out the size. She decides to make it 7 feet long and 5 feet wide.
items.prompt: Which equation shows how to solve for the size of the inside of the garden?
items.correct: Correct — area = length × width, measured in square feet.
items.hint: The inside of a flat shape is measured in square units.

items.title: Buying seeds
passage: Jayda goes to the store to buy seeds. She has $30.00 to spend, and each bag of seeds costs $6.00. She needs to figure out how to split up her money equally on the seeds so that she does not have any money left over.
items.prompt: Which key words tell you that this is a division problem?
items.hint: Which words mean sharing into equal groups?

items.title: Buying fertilizer
passage: Next, Jayda must figure out how much fertilizer she needs. She has to buy enough for her whole garden. Each bag of fertilizer covers 2 square feet of land.
items.prompt: Which steps explain what Jayda has to figure out before buying fertilizer?

options.text: 1. Find the area of her garden in square feet. 2. Divide the area by 2 square feet.
1. Count her money. 2. Divide the area of her garden by 2 square feet.
1. Find the perimeter of her garden. 2. Divide the area by 2 square feet.

items.correct: Correct — find the area, then divide by 2 sq ft per bag.
items.hint: Fertilizer covers the inside (area) of the garden.

items.title: Earning money for a fence
passage: Jayda wants to know if she can afford a $100 fence after one week of work. She works 5 days a week from 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM. She makes $8.50 per hour.
items.prompt: Which equation could Jayda use to figure out if she makes enough money in one week to buy the fence?
items.correct: Correct — 8 AM to 12 PM is 4 hours, 5 days a week.
items.hint: How many hours is 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM?

items.title: Boxes of fence
passage: Jayda must figure out how many boxes of fence material she needs to surround her whole garden so animals can't get in. Her garden is a rectangle that is 7 ft × 5 ft. Each box contains 6 feet of fence material.
items.prompt: Which answer choice shows the steps Jayda will follow to figure out how many boxes she needs?
items.correct: Correct — a fence goes around the garden (perimeter), then divide by 6 ft per box.
items.hint: A fence goes around the outside. Each box is 6 feet.

items.title: Two shovels on sale
passage: Jayda needs a shovel. Shovels are $8.50 each, but there is a sale: 2 shovels for $16. Jayda puts one shovel in her cart, but before she buys it she multiplies $8.50 × 2.
items.prompt: Why do you think Jayda multiplies $8.50 × 2?

options.text: to figure out if she will have enough money to buy the shovels
to figure out if both shovels will fit in her cart
to figure out how much money she would save if she buys two shovels on sale

items.correct: Correct — $8.50 × 2 = $17, so the $16 sale saves money.
items.hint: Compare two shovels at full price to the sale price.

items.title: Planting the rows
passage: Jayda has 4 rows, and each row holds 5 packages of seeds. She wants 10 pumpkin packages and 2 watermelon packages. With the rest, she wants an equal amount of tomato and corn packages. Step 1: 4 × 5 = 20 total spaces. Step 2: 10 + 2 = 12 packages. Step 3: 20 − 12 = 8. Step 4: 8 ÷ 2.
items.prompt: Why did Jayda complete the fourth step?

options.text: to figure out how far apart to plant the seeds
to figure out an equal amount of spaces for tomato and corn seeds
to find out how many total packages she could plant

items.correct: Correct — dividing the 8 leftover spaces by 2 gives equal tomato and corn packages.
items.hint: She wants the SAME number of tomato and corn packages.
